commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that salt is built from separate joined pairs, one sodium atom stuck to one chlorine atom.

fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: salt is a giant ionic lattice of sodium and chloride ions, and NaCl gives only the ratio.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say what the formula NaCl actually tells us and what structure the ions form.

commonErrors.misconception: Table salt is made of NaCl molecules.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner agrees with the student who says a grain of salt is one huge NaCl molecule.

fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: every ion belongs to the whole repeating lattice, surrounded by oppositely charged ions, so there is no single NaCl molecule to point at.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: give the one-sentence correction for the claim that a grain of salt is one huge molecule.

commonErrors.misconception: Table salt is made of NaCl molecules.

modelAnswers.answer: Each chlorine atom contributes one electron to a shared pair between the two atoms. Both atoms count the shared pair in their outer shell, so each has eight outer electrons. No electron is transferred, so no ions form.
modelAnswers.question: A chlorine molecule, Cl2, is held together by a covalent bond. Explain, in terms of electrons, how the bond forms and why no ions are made.

modelAnswers.answer: Magnesium loses its 2 outer electrons to form a positive magnesium ion, and oxygen gains 2 electrons to form a negative oxide ion. The bond is ionic.
modelAnswers.question: Magnesium has electron arrangement 2,8,2 and oxygen has 2,6. State the ions formed when they bond, and the type of bond.
